import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Pre-processing: Fill missing 'embarked' with the mode for better visualization
df['embarked'].fillna(df['embarked'].mode()[0], inplace=True)
df['embark_town'].fillna(df['embark_town'].mode()[0], inplace=True)

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a FacetGrid to show survival rates across multiple variables
g = sns.catplot(
    data=df,
    x='pclass',
    y='survived',
    hue='sex',
    col='embark_town',
    kind='bar',
    palette='viridis',
    height=5,
    aspect=0.8,
    errorbar=None # Hides confidence intervals for a cleaner look
)

# --- Improve Aesthetics and Labels ---

# Set a clear, overarching title for the entire figure
g.fig.suptitle('Titanic Survival Rate by Class, Sex, and Port of Embarkation', fontsize=16, y=1.03)

# Set custom titles for each subplot
g.set_titles("Port: {col_name}", size=12)

# Set axis labels
g.set_axis_labels("Passenger Class", "Survival Rate", size=12)

# Format the y-axis to show percentages
for ax in g.axes.flat:
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=1.0))
    ax.margins(y=0.1) # Add a little space at the top of the bars

    # Add annotations (percentage labels on top of each bar)
    for p in ax.patches:
        height = p.get_height()
        if height > 0: # Avoid annotating zero-height bars
            ax.annotate(f'{height:.0%}',
                        (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., height),
                        ha='center', va='bottom',
                        xytext=(0, 5),
                        textcoords='offset points',
                        fontsize=10)

# Adjust legend
g.legend.set_title("Sex")
sns.move_legend(g, "upper right", bbox_to_anchor=(.98, 0.9))

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
plt.close()
